original.description: The subject of this procurement proposal is the procurement of "Operations Engineering Services in support in ESEC/Redu" covering operational services for the preparation and execution of the mission operations entrusted to the Directorate of Operations located in ESEC, including the relevant Galileo Hosting Agreements.  ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are:  Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions")  Perform its In-Orbit activities.  Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations:   A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. The Small Satellites Mission Operations Centre is therefore responsible of the monitoring and control of the satellite and the corresponding ground segment, the handling of the user requests, the extraction of the mission products and their availability for distribution.  The Small Satellites operations concept relies on a highly automatic functioning of the ground segment and a high degree of autonomy in the space segment for the delayed execution of operations requested by telecommand and for satellite survival. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact.   This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities:  The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas.   The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel).  The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.

original.description: This activity aims to prepare a future in-orbit demonstrator of resilient PNT payload technologies based on digital and AI-enabled architectures. The study will investigate reconfigurable, software-defined payloads capable of characterizing and adapting to dynamic, congested or impaired RF environments.The activity will address the full signal chain, from generation to transmission, including onboard processing and AI-based techniques. A digital twin environment is also foreseen to be developed to support validation andperformance assessment.The objective is to mature concept and associated key payload technologies up to TRL 5/6 and deliver a credible, flight-representative architecture for next-generation PNT systems.

original.description: Objective: To develop a representative demonstrator of a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array with a reduced number of control points, by exploiting grating lobes.Description: For Earth Observation applications there are instruments, like Scatterometers, requiring a limited number of beams M pointing in fixed directions. A promising antenna architecture is based on an array antenna organized in interleaved subarrays (number of subarrays equal to the number of target beams M). Each subarray is having the periodic cell split in M sub-apertures. One of the M sub-apertures is occupied by a radiating element, the other M-1 slots are kept emptyto be used by the other M-1 interleaved subarrays. The dimension of the periodic cell is larger than one wavelength in order to create grating lobes exactly in the directions where the desired beams of the Scatterometer instrument are targeted. The array factor associated to the M phase centres of the M subarrays, when fed with identical phase value, creates a beam pointing at the boresight direction with radiative nulls positions coinciding with the grating lobes positions. Accordingly, when feeding the M inputs with thesame phase value a main beam in the boresight direction can be generated and the M-1 grating lobes can be cancelled by the radiative nulls. When feeding the M inputs with a linear phase in order to point the main beam exactly at one of the M possible targeted angles, the radiative nulls permit to cancel all the subarray pattern beams except the desired one. The M beams can be generated one atthe time, or simultaneously by adding a small beamforming MxM network. Possible values for M could be 3 or 5. To be noted also thatthecorresponding beams can be placed in the same azimuthal plane or not. This beamforming solution permits to reduce by a factor Mthe number of controls (phase shifters, direction couplers, amplifiers). As a consequence, a significant reduction in the cost and complexity of the entire instrument can be achieved. Reducing by a factor 3-5 the number of passive and active components in a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Instrument identification and requirements refinement. - Technology trade-off and down-selection. - Identification/optimization of most promising architectures. - Preliminary design of a baseline architecture and back-up architecture - Detailed design of a baseline architecture - Define preliminary manufacturing technique and prototype. - Definition of test and verification plan - Breadboard manufacturing and test - Results analysis and evaluation.

original.description: Development of a compact optical atomic clock module (physics package) for PNT applications. The activity will design, manufacture,and test an Engineering Model (EM) of a chip-scale optical clock exploiting an atomic optical transition to achieve 10 improved stability (target timing drift 10-30 ns/day) versus existing microwave clocks. The clock will provide a stabilized optical frequencyoutput in a low-power (< 5 W), compact device. Tasks include detailed thermo-mechanical design for robust operation in harsh environments, definition of low-power control electronics requirements and autonomous operation algorithms, assembly of the optical clock physics package, and development of Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) to control and test the EM. The EM will undergo performance verification in ambient and thermal conditions to demonstrate its stability, targeting TRL 4-5 and paving the way for future space-qualified ultra-stable timing solutions for navigation and timing systems.

original.description: This activity supports the evolution of European large (> 1 ton) LEO satellite platforms in line with ESA's Zero Debris objective by 2030. Building on previous work performed with European system integrators, it will mature platform designs from System Requirements Review (SRR) to Preliminary Design Review (PDR) level while advancing key Zero Debris technologies towards operational readiness.The activity will address end-of-life disposal, resilience against failures, health monitoring, and preparation for removal throughthe development and integration of innovative platform technologies. It will combine system-level platform design activities with technology maturation and co-engineering between platform integrators and specialised technology suppliers. The overall objective isto enable the next generation of European satellite product lines, supporting the implementation of the Space Debris Mitigation policy while maintaining technical feasibility, competitiveness, and affordability.
